sentences.text:
By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.34 of 2023 at Police Station-Jhunsi, District-Prayagraj under Sections 363, 366, 376, 323, 504, 506 IPC, Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act and Section 3(2) (5)
of SC/ST Act.
The applicant is in jail since 17.02.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 26.05.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Dheeraj Kumar Singh, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned A.G.A.-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. Learned counsel for the applicant has contested the minority of the victim as stated in the prosecution case.
2. The victim was shown as a minor of 12 years in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant contests the age of the victim set out in the prosecution case in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P.
and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and raises the following grounds:
(i). The school leaving certificate opines that the age of the victim is about 14 years and 4 months.

entities.text:
Monish Vs. State of U.P.
and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The age of the victim was incorrectly recorded in the said certificate by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.
However, the said school certificate is contradicted by the fact that the victim admits she is illiterate.
The age shown in the said certificate is unreliable.
The victim has made several contradictory statements in regard to her age which varies from 12 years to 15 years from time to time.

(ii). No medical examination to determine the correct age of the victim as per the latest scientific criteria and medical protocol by eminent doctors from a reputed institution was got done by the prosecution as it would falsify the prosecution case.
The victim is in fact a major.
4.
The victim and the applicant were intimate.
5. The F.I.R. is the result of parental opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship.

sentences.text: 6. The victim has stated in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that she stayed with the applicant at Magh Mela for three days.
However, the applicant never resisted the applicant nor did raise an alarm.
From her conduct it is evident that she was a consenting party.
7. Material contradictions in the F.I.R., statements of the victim under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and under Section 164 Cr.P.C. discredit the prosecution case.
8. Allegations have been made against the applicant only to deflect attention from her own conduct.

9. No medical report to corroborate the allegation of rape has been produced.
10. Prosecution does not connect the applicant with the offence.
11. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
12. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned A.G.A.-I points out that the applicant has one criminal case which has not been explained in the bail application.

Rejoining the issue and relying on the instructions received by the learned A.G.A., Shri Dheeraj Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant is a poor persons who is in jail.
The applicant does not have an effective pairokar.
Hence the details of the said cases could not be searched out and stated in the bail application in the first instance.

However, from the records available with the AGA and on instructions obtained from the applicant, it is contended that the applicant is a convenient scapegoat for the police to falsely implicate the applicant in the said case.
The said criminal case has no bearing on the instant case.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant-Shubham Nishad @ Honey be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number,
on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted."
